\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{धूलिः} (dhūliḥ)}{धूलिः (dhūliḥ)}]{\sk{धूलिः} (dhūliḥ) — dust}

\label{lesson:SA-C165-dhulih}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a playground, then the Sanskrit for an airport.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{धूलिः}}
\textbf{\sk{धूलिः}} — \emph{dhūliḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}dust\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dhūli} \textquotedblleft{}dust, powder, pollen\textquotedblright{} is inherited from Indo-European, with Latin \emph{fūlīgō} \textquotedblleft{}soot\textquotedblright{} as a cousin (EtymDB); MW queries a link with √dhū \textquotedblleft{}shake\textquotedblright{}. It lives on as Hindi \emph{dhūl} and Marathi \emph{dhūḷ} \textquotedblleft{}dust\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6835).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{aṅgāra} \textquotedblleft{}charcoal, a live coal\textquotedblright{} is old, in the Rigveda, and is inherited from Indo-European: MW sets it beside Lithuanian \emph{anglis} and Russian \emph{ugol'} \textquotedblleft{}coal\textquotedblright{}, and EtymDB agrees. \section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{लौहम्} (lauham)}{लौहम् (lauham)}]{\sk{लौहम्} (lauham) — iron}

\label{lesson:SA-C165-lauham}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a flame, then the Sanskrit for a live coal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{लौहम्}}
\textbf{\sk{लौहम्}} — \emph{lauham} — \textquotedblleft{}iron\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{lauha} is built from \emph{loha} \textquotedblleft{}red; copper; iron\textquotedblright{} with the first vowel strengthened (CDIAL 11172a): \textquotedblleft{}made of metal\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}iron\textquotedblright{}. MW connects \emph{loha} with a lost root meaning \textquotedblleft{}be red\textquotedblright{}, and CDIAL 11158 does too; \emph{loha} lives on as Hindi \emph{lohā} \textquotedblleft{}iron\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
